content:
In early July, Apple added basic search functionality to its TestFlight app. You might expect such a simple update to be well-received, but this same TestFlight update introduced a rather annoying bug for many users.

Personally, I was not significantly affected by this bug. For that reason, I initially thought this TestFlight update was a simple but meaningful improvement.

Sometimes, a small change can have a big impact. This is especially true for users with a large number of beta apps, and the latest TestFlight update is a prime example. Apple has just updated TestFlight for iPhone, iPad, Mac, and other platforms. The new version 4.3 adds a "search bar for quickly searching apps."

Looking back, I did notice something strange, which I noted at the bottom of the article (although at the time my understanding was completely the opposite):

I think the reason I didn't realize this was a bug is that I have kept all the TestFlight beta apps I've installed over the years, with the purpose of "merging" my originally separate iCloud and App Store Apple accounts. It's not a convenient arrangement, but for me it was worth it.

In any case, this TestFlight bug did not escape the notice of John Vorhees at MacStories:

So, you can imagine my excitement when I saw Zac Hall's article on 9to5Mac about TestFlight adding a search bar. I thought: "Finally!" I immediately put aside what I was working on and went to update the app. [...] Unfortunately, there's a big "but" to this story. Previously, TestFlight's beta versions were arranged in reverse chronological order, which I personally really liked. [...] Now, expired beta versions are mixed in alphabetically with the still-active TestFlight betas, and the list of expired betas seems to have expanded to include every beta I've ever participated in. I did a quick count, and for me it's roughly 800 app entries. As you can imagine, only a handful of those are actually valid betas. The search function does help, but scrolling is no longer a viable way to find things.

Then in August, John Gruber wrote about the TestFlight update and this bug on Daring Fireball:

Last night, more than a month after this bug appeared (and was pointed out by Vorhees), Apple finally updated TestFlight for the first time. Although the release notes only mention bug fixes, this update does indeed fix the relevant bug.

TestFlight version 4.3.1 is a fix for users affected by this regression issue.
